query: YouGov Economist poll Trump approval week

results.content: Donald Trump's popularity rebounded slightly in this week's Economist / YouGov Poll after his recent slump, but he remains deeply unpopular. This week's poll finds that 36% of Americans strongly or somewhat approve of Trump's job performance, and 57% disapprove — a net job approval of -21. That's an improvement for Trump from the week before, when 35% approved and 61% disapproved for a net approval of -26. Two weeks ago, Trump hit the lowest job approval numbers of either of his terms: 33%
results.title: Democrats have a double-digit lead among those who say they'll definitely vote in November

results.content:
Tuesday’s The Economist/YouGov poll came only a day after the president got less-than-stellar news from the newest Reuters/Ipsos poll released Aug. 24.

For the second week in a row, the poll found Trump’s approval rating sitting at 33%, the lowest approval rating the president has seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025. The numbers also tie Trump’s worst approval rating during his first term in office, in December 2017. [...] # Trump approval rating still hovering near record lows, new poll shows

Portrait of Fernando Cervantes Jr.

Despite a slight improvement in the polls for President Donald Trump, his approval rating continues to hover near record low
results.title: Trump approval rating still hovering near record lows, new poll shows

results.content:
Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to record or near-record lows, with support among middle-aged voters dropping sharply as economic concerns weigh heavily on his presidency. According to the Economist/YouGov poll conducted July 25-27, just 34% of U.S. adults approve of Trump’s job performance, tied for the lowest point of either his first or second term, while 62% disapprove, yielding a net approval rating of -28. [...] The Economist/YouGov — July 25-27, 2026 poll showing 34% approval (tied for record low), net approval of -28, and age-group breakdown with 45-64 year-olds at 33% approval and -29 net disapproval
